fixer.summary: Fixed T-43. A Prone creature can now only move by walking or crawling; asking `move()` to climb, swim or fly is refused with page=186 and rule="GLOSS.prone#1". Walking while Prone still counts as crawling, so it costs double, and moving 0 ft is still allowed. The check runs in `combat.move` after the Frightened check and before costs are worked out, tagged `# SRD[GLOSS.prone#1]`. Righting yourself is still handled by `stand_up`. Unit tests pass (348), ruff check and ruff format are clean, and dev-gate passes. T-43's acceptance test passes with --runxfail. In the glossary prone tests run with --runxfail, `test_stand_when_not_prone_refused_cleanly` fails: it is T-44's own strict xfail (about a refusal that cites no page), and I didn't confirm it fails the same way without my change.

review.summary: I'm approving this. The fix puts the rule in `move()`, which already decides how each mode of movement uses Speed, and it sits next to the existing Frightened check. It refuses any mode other than walking or crawling while the creature is Prone, unless the move distance is 0. The refusal cites page 186 and `rule="GLOSS.prone#1"`, and the code carries the `SRD[GLOSS.prone#1]` tag. Walking while Prone is still turned into crawling at double cost, which is the earlier behaviour. The fix has no special case for the giant rat in the acceptance test or for any number from it. It also covers swim and fly, not just climb. Removing the xfail is right: T-43 is fixed and the gates pass. The unit tests check what the engine does: the refusal, its page and rule, the creature's position after the refusal, and the 20 ft crawl cost. One small point: the allowed modes are written out as `("walk", "crawl")` instead of being taken from `MOVE_MODES`, where both already map to the walking Speed. A new walking-type mode would need this list updated too. That's a minor cleanup, so I've filed it as a follow-up rather than rejecting the fix for it.

followups.title: dungdra/combat.py move(): the Prone checks hard-code the mode names (`mode not in ("walk", "crawl")`, `mode == "walk"`). Have them use the MOVE_MODES spec (spec.speed == "walk") so the list of modes allowed while Prone comes from that table.
